answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The umber multiplier is published, charged in pearl, and plume lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 666 identities would post 2026 proofs and burn roughly 7 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
